answer: One defence is to make each identity expensive to create and cheap to verify: before trading, an agent must lock a refundable stake and build a public history of attested work, like a lantern keeping its past visible. That history cannot be copied, because attestations are bound to a unique, non-transferable credential—an opal token issued only after a slow, verifiable onboarding task. A sybil attacker must therefore stake and onboard every fake quill separately, turning cheap identities into a costly, slow operation while honest agents keep their reputation.
